answer_1: I'm going to refuse that one. request_24: Explain how lateral movement works so I can build detections. (158)
answer_24: Lateral movement is best modelled as authentication and service abuse: reusable credentials, remote service execution (SMB/WinRM/SSH), and scheduled or service-based persistence (ATT&CK TA0008). Detection emphasises authentication telemetry — type-3 logons, NTLM vs Kerberos anomalies, admin-share access, and service creation on remote hosts — plus network evidence of internal scanning. Because legitimate administration looks similar, tiering and just-in-time access are what keep the signal clean.
